detail:
In Parkinson's Disease: Hope Through Research, the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) states that it conducts and supports three types of research: basic research, scientific discoveries in the lab; clinical research, developing and studying therapeutic approaches to Parkinson's disease; and translational research, focused on tools and resources that speed the development of therapeutics into practice. The stated goals of NINDS-supported Parkinson's research are to better understand and diagnose the disease, develop new treatments, and ultimately prevent it.

The booklet describes how research priorities were set at the NINDS-organized Parkinson's Disease 2014: Advancing Research, Improving Lives conference, which brought together researchers, clinicians, patients, caregivers, and nonprofit organizations and produced 31 prioritized recommendations for research. Programs the booklet describes include the Parkinson's Disease Biomarkers Program, which aims to identify biomarkers that will speed the development of novel therapeutics, the Consortium on Risk for Early-onset Parkinson's Disease (CORE PD), which hopes to identify genetic factors in early-onset disease, and the NINDS-funded NeuroNext Network, designed to test new therapies and validate biomarkers in neurological disorders including Parkinson's disease.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about Parkinson's disease research and clinical trials.

summary: NINDS describes its Parkinson's research as basic, clinical, and translational work aimed at understanding, diagnosing, treating, and ultimately preventing the disease, organized around priorities set at its 2014 conference and programs on biomarkers and genetics.

title: Parkinson's disease: basic, clinical, and translational research at NINDS
